name: RAHL (Retrieval-Augmented Hierarchical in-Context Reinforcement Learning) with Hindsight Modular Reflection (HMR)
venue: arXiv:2408.06520 (cs.RO); published at IEEE ICRA 2025 (2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation), pp. 1217-1224, DOI 10.1109/ICRA55743.2025.11128105
authors_affiliation: Chuanneng Sun, Songjun Huang, Haiqiao Liu, Jie Gong, Dario Pompili. Rutgers University-New Brunswick (Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering; Dept. of Civil and Environmental Engineering), NJ, USA. (arXiv v1/v2 list Chuanneng Sun, Songjun Huang, Dario Pompili; the ICRA/Semantic Scholar record adds Haiqiao Liu and Jie Gong.)
code_url: N/A (no official code repository found via paper, arXiv links, or web search as of June 2026) [uncertain]
task_domain: Embodied / decision-making / task planning with LLMs; also tool-use-style web navigation and multi-hop QA. Evaluated on ALFWorld (embodied household), Webshop (web shopping), HotpotQA (multi-hop QA), plus a Boston Dynamics SPOT robot navigation demo.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-episode in-context reinforcement learning with a frozen LLM as policy (no gradient updates to the LLM). The agent operates over a retrieval-augmented goal-conditioned MDP: an LLM-based high-level policy decomposes a complex task into sub-goals on-the-fly, and a low-level policy generates actions to achieve each goal; a finisher module decides goal completion. Single-agent (though the high-/low-level policies and a finisher are distinct LLM roles). Supervision is via environment success signals across repeated episodes; learning is verbal (reflections) rather than parameter updates. Few-shot full-trajectory exemplars are provided per environment.
what_is_retrieved: Summarized verbal reflections (experiences) from previous sub-tasks/episodes: high-level reflections (over the sequence of proposed goals) and low-level reflections (over action sub-trajectories for each goal). Stored as key-value pairs (key = task/sub-task description, value = reflection).
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (long-term memory of past-episode reflections), populated online at test time. Few-shot exemplars are a separate static prompt component, but the retrieval store itself is the growing reflection memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: a fixed top-2 nearest-neighbor retrieval by embedding distance for both high- and low-level memories. No completeness/minimal-set objective and no adaptive/precision-driven variable-size selection.
retrieval_unit: Distilled reflection text (one or two sentences summarizing a failed/past trial), keyed by task or sub-task (goal) description. Two granularities: high-level reflection (about the goal sequence) and low-level reflection (about a goal's action sub-trajectory).
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced: long-term memory accumulates reflections generated after each episode during multi-episode deployment; it starts empty and grows. (Few-shot exemplars are static and human-provided, but are not the retrieved store.)
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index keyed by metadata/context: long-term memory split into two stores (high-level and low-level), each holding key-value pairs (key = task/sub-task description embedding, value = reflection text). No graph or hierarchical-category index beyond the two-level (high/low) separation.
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based nearest-neighbor): query and key embeddings are compared by distance; top-2 matches retrieved. Off-the-shelf embeddings; no learned/BM25/generative retriever. [uncertain] exact embedding model not specified in paper.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): retrieval is fixed similarity top-2 over embedding distance; the retriever is not trained or optimized by any task/LM/RL signal.
query_construction: Raw task or sub-task (goal) description used as the query; its embedding is computed and matched against stored keys. High-level memory queried with the task description; low-level memory queried with the sub-task/goal description.
query_granularity: Both (two-level retrieval): task-level query against high-level memory and sub-task/step-level (goal) query against low-level memory.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-sub-task: reflections are retrieved and injected into the prompt as new queries arrive to the high- or low-level memory during decision-making (i.e., when a new goal/sub-task is encountered), not only once at t=0.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the hierarchical control flow: a retrieval is triggered when a new query reaches high- or low-level memory (e.g., when proposing a new goal or working on a sub-task). Not confidence/attention/learned-classifier driven.
reranking: None: no reranking stage; top-2 nearest neighbors by embedding distance are used directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time (the retrieved reflections are already distilled summaries). The key refinement is upstream at write time: HMR distills failed trials into one or two short reflection sentences per module rather than storing raw trajectories. No post-retrieval rerank/compress/filter step.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved high- and low-level reflections are concatenated with the current state/trajectory (and few-shot examples) as input context to the frozen LLM policy. This is in-context RL (verbal feedback as a substitute for policy-gradient updates).
planning_integration: Hierarchical subtask-level, online/plan-as-you-go: the high-level LLM policy proposes sub-goals step-by-step (on-the-fly, conditioned on task + current-episode history) rather than planning all sub-tasks upfront; the low-level policy acts to satisfy each goal; a finisher decides when a goal is reached and triggers the next goal. Retrieval is interleaved at both the goal-proposal (high) and action (low) levels.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sub-task / per-goal (modular). Reflection and retrieval operate at the sub-trajectory (goal) level for the low-level policy and at the goal-sequence level for the high-level policy; within a goal, the agent uses ReAct-style [Think]/[Action] steps. Not per-token.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/guideline as free-text reflection (one or two natural-language sentences summarizing a past failed trial), injected verbatim into the prompt. Not raw trajectories, not programs, not latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight (verbal reflection) at two abstraction levels: high-level (about goal selection/sequencing) and low-level (about actions to achieve a goal). More abstract than a raw trajectory but tied to a specific task/sub-task key.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Modular reflection (HMR) itself is the main mechanism: reflecting on shorter sub-trajectories filters irrelevant information so the agent more accurately localizes errors, reducing noise from long trajectories. Tag-guided prompting injects structured prior to constrain generation. No explicit relevance evaluator, retriever-aware training, or distractor-filtering module.
memory_type: Episodic long-term memory (reflection store), split into high-level and low-level reflection memories, plus a short-term memory holding the current-episode trajectory.
write_back: true. After each (failed) episode, HMR summarizes the trial into short high- and low-level reflections that are written into the corresponding long-term memory as key-value pairs for use in future episodes.
online_growth: Yes: long-term reflection memory grows during multi-episode deployment/test-time; it is not frozen after an offline induction phase.
write_back_trigger: Reflective and failure-driven: at the end of an episode, when the trial fails, the agent generates verbal reflections (summarized into one or two sentences per module) and stores them in long-term memory. Writes are essentially triggered on failure (to drive next-episode improvement) via the hindsight reflection step.
failure_experience_usage: Failure-focused corrective reflections: failed trials are summarized into reflections stored in memory and retrieved to guide future trials; the framework explicitly reflects on what went wrong (no contrastive success-vs-failure pairing described; emphasis is on correcting failures).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only: reflections from each episode are added to long-term memory; the paper does not describe dedup/merge, delta-update, overwrite, or pruning of stored reflections. [uncertain] (no explicit forgetting/merging mechanism stated).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/case-selection is fixed similarity top-2, not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval policy. (RAHL is described as a deterministic decision policy with HMR acting as the analog of a policy-gradient update, but the retrieval mechanism itself is not learned.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent private memory. The high-level policy, low-level policy, and finisher are roles of one agent/system; memory is not shared across multiple distinct agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 scenarios across six task types), Webshop, HotpotQA (Wikipedia-based multi-hop QA). Additional hardware demonstration on a Boston Dynamics SPOT robot (navigation to a person in an adjacent room) using GPT-4-turbo as image analyst and GPT-4o as decision-maker.
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld); web (Webshop); multi-hop QA (HotpotQA). Plus a real-robot embodied navigation demo (SPOT).
baselines: Retroformer (gradient-based, LoRA rank=4 on a separate reflection LM), ADaPT (as-needed decomposition + planning), Reflexion (full-trajectory verbal reflection over ReAct), ExpeL (experience storage/retrieval + insight rule set). Default LLM back-end GPT-3.5-turbo (with GPT-4 / GPT-4o variants studied).
key_metrics: Success rate (%) per environment, reported at episode 1 (Pass@1) and at 5 episodes; results averaged over ten runs with confidence intervals.
headline_result: At 5 episodes, RAHL improves success rate by 9% on ALFWorld, 42% on Webshop (new state-of-the-art), and 10% on HotpotQA over strong baselines (GPT-3.5-turbo). Table I: Webshop #Epi=5 RAHL 83% vs Retroformer 36% / ADaPT 28% / Reflexion 28% / ExpeL 41%; ALFWorld #Epi=5 RAHL 87% (Retroformer 100%); HotpotQA #Epi=5 RAHL 57%.
ablations: Ablation variants sharing the same first episode: (1) RAHL-Retry (raw past failed full trajectories with no reflection; terminates early by exceeding LLM max sequence length); (2) RAHL-Reflexion (full-trajectory reflection instead of modular); (3) RAHL w/o Tag (LLM freely chooses next step without [Goal]/[Think]/[Action]/[Finish] tag guidance). Findings: tag guidance is helpful (w/o Tag underperforms); verbal reflection (HMR or Reflexion) beats raw-trajectory retry and is more scalable; HMR (modular sub-trajectory reflection) outperforms full-trajectory Reflexion, especially in long-trajectory / text-heavy ALFWorld and HotpotQA. LLM-backend study: GPT-4 helps ALFWorld/Webshop; GPT-3.5 with GPT-4 HMR beats GPT-3.5 and even beats GPT-4 on HotpotQA.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end task success rates are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (success rate). Process quality is addressed qualitatively/indirectly (HMR localizes errors better; tags improve interpretability; goal trajectories shown), but no quantitative step-wise retrieval/planning accuracy or trajectory-quality metric is reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency framed mainly via reflection scalability and context length: HMR reflects on shorter sub-trajectories to improve reflection efficiency and avoid exceeding the LLM max sequence length (a failure mode of RAHL-Retry), and to better localize errors. No quantitative report of retrieval call counts, API cost, latency, token counts, or speedup numbers. [uncertain] (no explicit cost numbers).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: top-2 reflections retrieved from each of high- and low-level memory and injected into the prompt. Few-shot exemplars: two full successful trajectories for Webshop/HotpotQA; two task-specific examples per each of six ALFWorld tasks; plus two goal-trajectory reflection examples and one full-trajectory reflection example. No adaptive-k or budget-capped selection beyond the fixed top-2 and these exemplar counts.
builds_on: Reflexion (verbal reflection / closed-loop in-context RL), ReAct (Think-then-Act reasoning traces as the low-level actor pattern), ExpeL (experience storage and embedding-based retrieval from memory), goal-conditioned Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) and Hindsight ideas (e.g., HAC 'Learning multi-level hierarchies with hindsight', option-critic), and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
contrasts_with: Reflexion (full-trajectory reflection vs HMR modular sub-trajectory reflection), ADaPT (upfront task decomposition before execution vs RAHL's on-the-fly online goal generation, and no multi-episode policy improvement), RT-H (hierarchical but no policy improvement after first episode), Retroformer (gradient-based reflection-LM fine-tuning vs RAHL's frozen-LLM verbal in-context updates), classic HRL methods HAC and option-critic (language-integrated learning vs gradient-based hierarchies).
lineage: Group F (decision/memory RL): goal-conditioned hierarchical in-context RL with a growing episodic reflection memory. Sits in the Reflexion/ExpeL lineage of experience-/reflection-based in-context RL agents, extending it with (a) hierarchical high-/low-level goal-conditioned policy structure and (b) modular hindsight reflection retrieved as cross-episode augmentation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (yes, embedding top-2), Reuse (yes, reflections injected into prompt), Revise (partial: HMR revises/refines experiences into reflections at write time, not by adapting a retrieved case during solving), Retain (yes, reflections stored to long-term memory). Flags: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise(partial), Retain].
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it frames itself via HRL + RAG + verbal reflection (Reflexion/ExpeL lineage), realizing CBR-like retrieve/reuse/retain mechanics under different terminology.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill index; retrieved items are verbal reflections, not tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure design; reflections are short and stored/retrieved directly as key-value pairs).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol such as RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling; environments are interacted with via their native text action spaces).
adaptation_mechanism: Verbal in-context reuse: retrieved reflections are injected verbatim into the prompt to steer the frozen LLM's next-episode behavior. Adaptation of experience happens at write time via hindsight modular reflection (summarizing failures into corrective guidance) rather than per-query case rewriting; no execution-feedback case-rewriting or RL fine-tuning of reuse.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary research paper, not a survey/taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks: ALFWorld 134 scenarios over six task types; HotpotQA ~113K QA pairs; Webshop; not a new benchmark contribution).
